jobs.description:
About the Organization

Bay Area Disc (BADA)’s mission is to serve, strengthen, and grow the Ultimate community by creating opportunities for athletes of all ages and backgrounds to interact, develop, and compete. Central to everything we do is the Spirit of the Game, a philosophy that emphasizes integrity, respect, and joy in play.
BADA is more than just a sports organization. We believe in the transformative power of Ultimate as a tool for personal and community development. Ultimate isn’t just a game—it’s a vehicle for fostering connections, building character, and promoting inclusivity. Through Ultimate, players learn teamwork, leadership, and conflict resolution skills, all within a fun and supportive environment.
We serve a diverse community across the Bay Area, from young beginners taking their first steps on the field to seasoned adult players looking to refine their skills. Our programs offer a mix of recreational and competitive opportunities, creating spaces where everyone can find their place, whether they’re in it for the joy of casual play or the thrill of high-level competition. In addition to hosting our own leagues and tournaments, we partner with other organizations to expand access and foster even more opportunities for engagement.
Our vision is a Bay Area full of healthy, thriving, compassionate, and skilled individuals who live in strong, inclusive, equitable, and interconnected communities. By using Ultimate as our medium, we aim to cultivate these outcomes, shaping a future where people not only play together but grow together.
At the heart of BADA are our core values: Fun, Respect, Community, and Belonging.
These values guide our programs and initiatives, ensuring that we create environments where everyone feels welcomed and valued.
Bay Area Disc is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to making a positive impact through sport, using Ultimate as a unique and powerful catalyst for change.

As the governing body that supports the sport in the region, we directly host leagues, tournaments and teams (often divided into youth and adult opportunities, with a mix of recreational and competitive opportunities), as well as partnering with other organizations to foster additional playing opportunities.

We envision a Bay Area full of healthy, thriving, compassionate, and skilled individuals who live in strong, inclusive, equitable, and interconnected communities. We use the unique sport of Ultimate to improve individuals and communities, creating the future we want to see.

About the Role

As the Executive Director of the organization, you’ll lead the entire nonprofit towards accomplishing its important mission and goals. Serving as the external face of BADA, the ED partners closely with the Board, the ultimate community, and the broader Bay Area community to secure and allocate the resources necessary to maintain the health of the organization and expand its programmatic impact. 
Reporting to the President of the Board, the Executive Director (ED) is the lead staff member who holds overall strategic, financial and operational responsibility for organization. This includes the management of the Bay Area Disc Association staff, fundraising, operations, donor cultivation, community engagement and organizational vision + development. The ED drives and is accountable for the execution of BADA’s strategic priorities and fulfillment of its core commitments. 
BADA has been serving the community since 2009, and was registered as its own 501c3 in 2018. The nonprofit is at a pivotal point in its maturity journey, and we’re excited for the impact that this role will have in leading an exciting new chapter, especially as we look to grow revenue through programming, grant, and donor funding, building on our strong programming base, so we can expand programming, deepen financial aid, and reach players and communities we don't yet serve.
BADA facilitates over 100 events annually, with approximately 5,000 youth and adult participants each year. These events range from local leagues and tournaments to community clinics and youth programs, providing opportunities for players of all skill levels. Our growth goals are deeply woven into our ongoing DEIB (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging) work, and we are centering inclusivity and accessibility as we move into the next phase. We currently have a team of 3 full time staff, with a broad network of contractors and volunteers supporting these initiatives as well. These folks all either directly or indirectly will report into this ED position.
This role is approximately 50% development, fundraising, strategic visioning to drive the organization forward, 25% internal operations, staffing + fiscal management, 25% programming + community engagement.

Skills and Experience

As we approach this search, we know that there are a lot of potential paths that could lead someone to being successful in this role. We value all experience (educational, lived, professional, etc.) and encourage anyone who is passionate about this opportunity to apply - regardless of whether or not they meet the listed core competencies that we’re looking for.

Deputy Director, Portfolio Management

Classification: 0904 - Mayoral Staff XVI

Department: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)

Reports To: Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development Director

Reporting directly to the MOHCD Director, the Deputy Director, Portfolio Management provides executive leadership for the City’s long-term stewardship of its publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and ensures equitable access to all City-sponsored affordable housing. The Deputy Director establishes strategic direction for asset management, affordable housing occupancy and placement, Inclusionary Housing policy, portfolio preservation, and regulatory compliance to ensure the long-term financial, physical, and operational success of the City’s affordable housing investments. The role also ensures that residents have safe, healthy homes that support the social, physical, and economic well-being of tenants and homeowners.

As a member of MOHCD’s Senior Leadership Team, the Deputy Director collaborates with executive staff to develop and implement agency priorities, establish organizational strategy, and advance policies that efficiently preserve and strengthen San Francisco’s affordable housing portfolio.

The Deputy Director provides executive oversight of the Portfolio Management Division that includes 25 staff members.

Additionally, The Deputy Director Directly Supervises Two Senior Leaders

Director of Inclusionary Programs and Housing Placement

The Director of Inclusionary Programs and Housing Placement is responsible for administering the City’s Inclusionary Housing rental programs, affordable housing marketing and lease-up activities, housing placement operations, and related occupancy functions. The Director oversees implementation of affirmative marketing requirements, resident selection processes, housing lotteries, and implementation of affordable housing preference legislation, policies, and procedures. The Director ensures occupancy procedures are compliant with local laws governing access to affordable housing and are equitable, transparent, efficient, and consistent across all affordable housing and homeownership opportunities.

The Director also provides executive oversight of the Database for Affordable Housing Listings, Information and Applications (DAHLIA) San Francisco’s affordable housing portal, and associated business processes supporting affordable housing marketing, application processing, resident placement, lotteries, and occupancy administration to ensure equitable outcomes for San Franciscans seeking affordable housing. The Director collaborates with affordable housing developers, property management companies, community-based organizations, and City departments to ensure consistent implementation of City housing policies and regulatory requirements including Fair Housing and the American Disability Act.

Director of Asset Managemen
t

The Director of Asset Management provides leadership for the long-term stability of over 36,000 rental and 3,000 homeownership units. The Director ensures financial and physical stewardship of MOHCD’s publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and works closely with project sponsors’ compliance staff to ensure the sustainability of all City sponsored affordable housing. Responsibilities include oversight of asset management, portfolio financial performance, multifamily loan servicing, capital planning, reserve management, multifamily refinancing and restructuring, rehabilitation planning, portfolio data management, financial risk assessment, and regulatory compliance. The Director develops strategies that preserve affordability, improve property performance, protect public investment, and support the long-term sustainability of the City’s affordable housing portfolio.

Role description

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The Deputy Director’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Serve as a member of MOHCD’s Senior Leadership Team, providing executive leadership on agency priorities, strategic initiatives, and organizational management.
Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for the 25-person Portfolio Management Division, ensuring alignment with MOHCD’s mission, priorities, and affordable housing objectives.
Supervise Director-level managers responsible for major programs and ensure effective coordination across all functional areas.
Establish division-wide goals, performance expectations, and operational priorities and efficiencies while fostering collaboration across all Portfolio Management functions.
Develop and implement equitable policies that strengthen long-term stewardship of the City’s affordable housing portfolio and improve organizational effectiveness while balancing the needs of the communities living in affordable housing.
Expand, standardize, and improve communication regarding City sponsored affordable housing operations, regulations and requirements among project sponsors, tenants and owners.
Oversee the long-term financial and physical performance of the City’s publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and direct strategies that preserve affordability, protect public investment, and promote high-quality housing.
Provide executive oversight of affordable housing occupancy, marketing, lease-up, resident placement, housing lotteries, housing preference implementation, and DAHLIA operations to ensure equitable, transparent, and efficient administration of City affordable housing programs.
Direct policies governing inclusionary policy implementation, asset management, regulatory compliance, occupancy administration, resident selection, and portfolio preservation.
Oversee multifamily portfolio-related financing, recapitalization, rehabilitation planning, reserve management, and other long-term preservation initiatives.
Coordinate with affordable housing and private developers, property management companies, lenders, realtors, investors, regulatory agencies, community-based organizations, and other City departments to advance transparent affordable housing policy and operational excellence.
Represent MOHCD before the Mayor, Board of Supervisors, City commissions, community organizations, industry partners, and the public on portfolio performance, housing placements and operations, and inclusionary policy, as necessary.
Identify emerging operational, financial, legislative, and regulatory issues affecting the City’s affordable housing portfolio and its residents and recommend strategic policy and management solutions.
Promote innovation, accountability, equity, and continuous improvement across all Portfolio Management programs and operations.
Perform related duties as assigned.

How to qualify

Provide strong leadership, manage subordinate staff, exercise effective judgment in critical/emergency situations, analyze complicated and sensitive issues, and communicate and provide options clearly to the Mayor, Mayoral staff, commissions, boards, committees, other agencies and the public. Apply the principles of public administration, financial and personnel management and effectively interpret all applicable laws, ordinances and codes. Exercise independent analysis, adaptability and judgment on specialized proposals with difficult, complicated options. Effectively present Mayor's policies and opinions to outside entities such as the public, boards, commissions and government agencies. Deputy Director,
Multifamily Housing and Homeownership Programs

Classification: 0904 Mayoral Staff XVI

Department: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)

Reports To: Mayor's Office of Housing and Community Development Director

Reporting directly to the MOHCD Director, the Deputy Director, Multifamily Housing and Homeownership Programs
provides executive leadership for the City’s affordable multifamily housing production, preservation, housing finance, construction oversight, and homeownership programs. In coordination with the Director, the Deputy Director establishes the strategic direction for these program areas, oversees policy development and implementation, and advances innovative financing and programmatic initiatives that expand affordable housing opportunities and sustainable homeownership throughout San Francisco.

The Deputy Director provides executive oversight of the Homeownership and Multifamily Rental Housing Division that includes 38 staff members.

Additionally, the Deputy Director provides direct supervision to 5 Director-level leadership staff responsible for these major program areas:

New Construction
Acquisition and Preservation
Housing Finance
Homeownership Programs
Construction Representation

New Construction

MOHCD’s New Construction Program is led by a Director who manages a team of project managers and loan administrators responsible for developing 100 percent affordable housing throughout San Francisco. Responsibilities include underwriting projects for approval by the Citywide Loan Committee and Board of Supervisors; overseeing affordable housing development partners during programming, predevelopment, construction, marketing, and lease-up; administering the City’s Land Dedication Program; and closing construction and permanent financing.

Acquisition and Preservation

The Acquisition and Preservation Program is led by a Director responsible for financing the acquisition, rehabilitation, and long-term preservation of affordable multifamily housing. The program oversees refinancing and restructuring of existing affordable housing developments, administers the Small Sites Program, coordinates acquisition financing strategies, and partners with nonprofit developers, lenders, and public agencies to preserve affordable housing throughout the City.

Housing Finance

The Housing Finance Director is responsible for coordinating MOHCD’s multifamily financing and underwriting activities, including affordable housing revenue bonds, loan structuring, lending policies, capital financing strategies, and funding procurements. The Director evaluates federal, state, and local financing opportunities to maximize affordable housing resources and develops policies that strengthen the City’s affordable housing investment strategies.

Homeownership Programs

MOHCD’s Homeownership Programs are led by a Director responsible for the City’s affordable homeownership initiatives, including Inclusionary ownership programs within market rate housing and the sale and re-sale of Below Market Rate (BMR) units, first-time homeowner assistance programs, and related affordable homeownership opportunities. The Director oversees the secondary lending activities and administration of all homebuyer and homeowner loan programs including loan servicing of approximately 850 market rate property loans. Creating an average of 200 new first-time homeowners each year, the Director oversees the implementation of all homeownership programs generated by the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) and other affordable homeownership initiatives designed to expand equitable access to homeownership. The Director works closely with the Homeownership Compliance Manager to ensure households purchasing market rate housing with City assistance remain program eligible throughout their ownership. The Director develops and implements policies, oversees program operations, and collaborates with lenders, nonprofit organizations, developers, community-based organizations, and public agencies to advance the City’s affordable homeownership goals.

Construction Representation

A Senior Construction Representative manages a team of construction professionals responsible for evaluating MOHCD-funded projects throughout all phases of development to ensure cost efficiency, constructability, and compliance with program and design standards. The team monitors projects during construction through project closeout and works collaboratively with project sponsors and regulatory agencies to resolve development issues.

Role description

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The Deputy Director’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Serve as a member of MOHCD’s Senior Leadership Team, providing executive leadership on agency priorities, strategic initiatives, and organizational management.
Provide executive leadership for the City’s multifamily housing production, acquisition, preservation, housing finance, and homeownership programs.
Establish strategic direction and organizational priorities for the Division.
Supervise Director-level managers responsible for major housing program operations and ensure effective coordination across all functional areas.
Manage MOHCD’s affordable housing pipeline by coordinating multifamily pipeline budget review meetings, maintaining up to date the multifamily budget projections, and overseeing the strategic allocation of local, state, and federal funding resources supporting affordable homeownership and multifamily housing production and preservation.
Develop and implement policies, funding strategies, and innovative financing approaches that expand affordable housing production, preservation, and homeownership opportunities.
Oversee the review and approval process for new construction, acquisition, preservation, housing finance, and homeownership funding recommendations, ensuring timely executive review and successful approval by the Citywide Loan Committee and Board of Supervisors.

Position Summary

Our Lady Queen of Angels Catholic Church seeks a creative, organized, and mission-driven Director of Communications & Digital Media to lead and manage all parish communications efforts across print, digital, social media, video, email, and web platforms.

The Director of Communications & Digital Media will oversee parish branding, social media strategy, multimedia production, website management, digital engagement, and weekly parish communications. Another aspect of this roll would be administrative assistant to the pastor. This would include, scheduling for the pastor, screening calls, emails and other administrative tasks as necessary for the pastor.

The ideal candidate is a strong communicator, creative storyteller, skilled multimedia producer, and collaborative team member with a passion for parish life and Catholic evangelization.

part of The Pennant Group family, is currently seeking entrepreneurial leaders with proven results in building and leading exceptional teams and has a passion for the senior living industry. Join us in making an impact and shaping the future of senior care!

About The Opportunity

The CEO-in-Training (CIT) Program is designed to prepare outstanding leaders for an opportunity to run one of our assisted living, independent living, or memory care communities. This salaried, full-time training program typically lasts 3–6 months, depending on your background and experience. CITs may advance to lead one of our thriving communities or future acquisition, with continued mentorship and operational support from experienced partners.

As a CIT, you will gain hands-on practical experience in operations, clinical care, and business management under the guidance of an experienced Executive Director/CEO. The program offers mentorship, cross-functional training, and real responsibility in a dynamic environment. You’ll learn to drive results, cultivate a strong team culture, and develop a deep understanding of the unique business models that power Pennant’s success.

Key Responsibilities

Engage in immersive, on-the-job training across operational, care, and administrative functions
Shadow department heads and front-line staff to understand the day-to-day rhythm of community life
Take the lead on real-time projects and contribute to meaningful improvements within your host community
Study relevant state regulations and best practices in senior living operations
Align leadership and interpersonal skills with Pinnacle’s core values and mission

Qualifications

Minimum Requirements:

3–5 years of leadership experience in any industry

Position Overview:
The responsibility of the Executive Director is to develop strategic partnerships and raise the money to achieve Project C.U.R.E.’s mission of delivering life-saving medical relief to the neediest people in the world. This is a fundraising position with an annual goal of $1.25 million.

Responsibilities include developing productive donor relationships with individuals, corporations and organizations that have financial resources, executing successful fundraising events, and engaging the local community to support the work of Project C.U.R.E. around the world.

Responsibilities:

•Design and execute an effective, quantifiable fundraising plan for individual giving, major gifts, corporate donations, foundation support and C.U.R.E. Cargo sponsors from the Phoenix community and region.
•Recruit and lead the Phoenix Ambassador Board, which is an engaged, active group of individuals who assist and advise the Executive Director in fundraising and development of the mission of Project C.U.R.E.
•Develop and manage strategic partnerships with organizations and companies as well as university programs, hospital partners, faith communities, and others; solicit funding, grants and gifts for Project C.U.R.E.’s projects around the world.
•Secure financial sponsors for individual container delivery projects through the C.U.R.E. Cargo program, and serve as the primary “Client Care” steward of that relationship throughout the project.
•Recruit and manage a team of volunteers and interns, including members of the Ambassador Board to expand the effectiveness of the Executive Director’s efforts.
•Collaborate with the Phoenix Operations Director who manages the procurement, warehousing, transportation, processing and delivery of life-saving medical supplies and equipment.
•Execute fundraising events in coordination with the Director of Special Events through securing financial and gift-in-kind sponsorships, donor attendance and event execution.
•Represent Project C.U.R.E. in the news and on social media as well as attend community events to increase the recognition and reputation of Project C.U.R.E. in the community.
•Coordinate with staff at the International Headquarters and the other Executive Directors in C.U.R.E. Communities by sharing stories and “best practices,” attending semi-annual Town Hall meetings in Denver, Colorado and participating in regularly scheduled meetings and conference calls.
•Manage accurate and up-to-date information on donors and other project sponsors in the Project C.U.R.E. (CRM) database.

Qualifications:
The Executive Director must demonstrate alignment with Project C.U.R.E.’s mission and core values, and possess the internal motivation and passion to address the healthcare inequalities in the developing world in a sustainable manner.

The ideal candidate for the position demonstrates the following qualities:
Is qualified:
Holds a bachelor’s degree and has at least five years of demonstrated fundraising success, specifically in the area of individual giving and major gifts.
Is goal oriented: Manages to metrics, OKR’s and Key Performance Indicators, including meeting or exceeding fundraising goals/objectives, monitoring performance and reporting results; is a “self-starter” who is internally motivated and does not require significant supervision.
Develops people: Recruits, inspires and leads volunteers, mentees and interns to achieve goals within the context of building a “performance culture.” Is accessible to volunteers and associates at all levels, interacting consistently, openly and honestly to assure everyone is treated with dignity and respect.
Works well with others: Utilizes excellent relationship management and interpersonal skills; the ability to work effectively with donors, board members, volunteers, staff and interns; displays mature judgment, high emotional intelligence and effective communication skills.
Is resourceful & “bottom line” oriented: To continue to meet the efficiency goals of Project C.U.R.E., the Executive Director must secure in-kind sponsorships and leverage relationships to reduce direct expenses by negotiating discounts and benefits with vendors and venues, and can meet budget and resource challenges to maximize net revenue goals.
Is a recognized leader: Continually seeks learning and self-improvement, maintains the highest ethical standards and values, and encourages others toward higher levels of effectiveness.
Is a capable communicator: Demonstrates effective communication skills in writing, interpersonal communication and public speaking; understands the importance of listening.
Is motivated: Has an obvious passion and enthusiasm for saving lives and strengthening health infrastructure systems in the developing world with an attitude of tenacity and determination.
Is well organized: Is prepared, conscientious, effective and able to prioritize in an environment
with multiple demands and complicated schedules.
Is coachable: Has an attitude of openness, is eager to learn new things without becoming defensive, and does not get stuck in a repetitive pattern of doing the same things the same way for too long. Can quickly comprehend complex concepts and will accept instruction.

Compensation & Benefits:
This position offers competitive compensation commensurate with experience and typically ranges from $95,000 to $110,000 annually. The position includes a generous health insurance plan, paid vacation and holidays, and a 403(b) plan.

About Us
: Healthcare in many developing countries is a global crisis. The severe lack of healthcare disrupts social and economic stability in almost every developing nation. Disease causes nine-out-of-ten preventable deaths in developing nations among children and adults. Millions of children under the age of five die each year from preventable disease, and more than 70% of these deaths occur from pneumonia, diarrhea, measles, malaria and malnutrition.

Founded in 1987, Project C.U.R.E. (www.projectcure.org) has grown to be the largest organization in the world delivering nearly 200+ forty-foot ocean freight cargo containers of donated medical supplies and equipment annually. Each project begins with an onsite Needs Assessment to ensure that Project C.U.R.E. delivers the right items to the right people. Project C.U.R.E. has delivered medical relief in 130+ countries. In addition, Project C.U.R.E. conducts C.U.R.E. Clinics, Helping Babies Breathe trainings, and bio-technical trainings to hospitals and health care clinics in 40 developing nations.

On average, the value of a Project C.U.R.E. Cargo container is worth $450,000 (wholesale), providing an amazing 20-to-1 “return on investment." Project C.U.R.E. operates Distribution Centers in Denver, Phoenix, Houston, Nashville, Philadelphia, Kansas City and Chicago where 20,000+ volunteers sort more than 26,000 types of non-perishable medical supplies and certify medical equipment for shipment abroad.

Project C.U.R.E. also operates 9 Collection Centers from Ithaca to Sarasota and Portland. Project C.U.R.E. receives both new and quality used medical items from hundreds of hospitals throughout the United States and medical manufacturers, such as Stryker, Medline, Medtronic, Kimberly-Clark, Steris, and Hill-Rom.

Project C.U.R.E. operates on 2.5% administrative overhead and has earned numerous awards for being the industry leader in international medical donations. Project C.U.R.E. is recognized as a four-star organization by Guidestar, ranked a Platinum Participant by Charity Navigator and was ranked by Forbes magazine as one of the 20 most cost effective nonprofits in the United States.

Mission:
The mission of Project C.U.R.E. is to identify, solicit, collect, sort and distribute medical supplies and services according to the imperative needs of the world.

Ocean of Wisdom School (OWS) is a new K–4 public charter school preparing to open in Minnesota in Fall 2027, with a planned expansion to K–8.

OWS will combine rigorous, standards-aligned academics with Social, Emotional, and Ethical (SEE) Learning, fostering academic excellence, compassion, resilience, ethical decision-making, and a strong sense of belonging. The school will also incorporate Tibetan language and cultural learning as part of its globally grounded, culturally responsive educational model.

OWS is currently in its founding phase. We are seeking a Founding Executive Director to help turn this vision into a thriving school.

The Opportunity

As OWS's Founding Executive Director, you will have the extraordinary opportunity to shape a school's culture, community, and educational experience from the very beginning.

Working closely with the Board of Directors, the Founding Executive Director will lead OWS through the transition from planning to opening and establish the foundation for long-term success. The role combines educational leadership with organizational development, staffing, operations, financial management, enrollment, and community engagement.

The ideal candidate is energized by building something new, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and able to move between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution.

School Leadership & Development

Lead the development and successful launch of OWS for Fall 2027.
Translate the school's mission and vision into effective educational and organizational practices.

Educational Leadership

Establish the operational systems necessary to launch and operate the school.
Oversee compliance, contracts, vendors, risk management, and school-opening requirements.
Develop and manage the annual budget and maintain strong financial controls.
Support grants, fundraising, and other resource-development efforts.

Enrollment & Community

Develop student recruitment and enrollment strategies.
Build strong relationships with prospective and enrolled families.
Develop partnerships with educational, cultural, nonprofit, and community organizations.
Serve as a public representative and advocate for OWS.

Job Description

CEO/General Manager

Gem City Market – Dayton, Ohio

Retained Search Partner: The Carlisle Group

Salary Range: $90,000 – $115,000

The Carlisle Group is pleased to be partnered on a retained search with Gem City Market
in Dayton, Ohio, in the search for their next CEO/General Manager
.

Gem City Market is a community-centered, full-service grocery cooperative created to bring quality, affordable food to a diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood in Dayton. More than simply a grocery store, Gem City Market is committed to being a pillar of the community it serves—helping strengthen the local culture, creating opportunity, and providing a welcoming place where neighbors can shop, connect, and thrive.

The co-op is seeking an entrepreneurial, community-minded grocery leader who can balance mission and margin
—someone who understands that a successful cooperative must deliver both meaningful community impact and strong financial performance. The CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to lead the Market into its next chapter while ensuring that customers receive quality products at affordable prices in a clean, welcoming, and inclusive environment.

Living in Dayton

Dayton offers an appealing combination of affordability, accessibility, community, and opportunity
. Located in southwest Ohio, Dayton provides the amenities of a larger metropolitan area while retaining a strong sense of neighborhood and community.

The city has a rich history of innovation, entrepreneurship, and community involvement and is home to a diverse collection of neighborhoods, restaurants, arts and cultural attractions, parks, and outdoor recreation. Residents enjoy access to an extensive regional park system, the great Miami River, biking and hiking trails, and numerous opportunities to enjoy the outdoors.

Dayton's location is another advantage. Cincinnati and Columbus are both within approximately an hour's drive, while Cleveland and Indianapolis are accessible within a few hours. The region offers a relatively affordable cost of living compared with many larger U.S. metropolitan areas, making Dayton an attractive place to build both a career and a life.

For a leader who wants to make a tangible difference in a community while enjoying a high quality of life, Dayton presents a compelling opportunity.

Position Purpose

The CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading Gem City Market as a successful, financially sustainable cooperative while advancing the goals and purposes established by the Board of Directors.

The CEO/General Manager Will Ensure That The Market

Operates efficiently and ultimately profitably.
Provides quality, affordable groceries that meet the needs of its customers.
Maintains a clean, welcoming, and inclusive shopping environment.
Builds a positive culture for employees and the broader community.
Advances the cooperative's mission and role as a community institution.
Remains responsive to the needs of the diverse, low- to moderate-income neighborhood it serves.

The CEO/General Manager will bring together the disciplines of grocery operations, financial management, merchandising, people leadership, marketing, and community engagement
to ensure the continued success of Gem City Market.

Overview Of Responsibilities

Operations

Lead an efficient, customer-focused, and ultimately profitable cooperative grocery operation.
Create a positive store atmosphere and build a motivated, accountable staff team.
Maintain current knowledge of grocery retailing, industry trends, and best practices, particularly those applicable to cooperative markets and urban, low- to moderate-income communities.
Develop and maintain productive relationships with market partners, wholesale distributors, local markets, and other industry resources.
Establish and maintain an appropriate product mix that meets shopper needs while supporting financial objectives.
Develop and execute a margin strategy that allows Gem City Market to remain price competitive while maintaining adequate cash flow.
Ensure compliance with all applicable laws, regulations, licenses, permits, health requirements, and employment standards.
Continuously evaluate operational performance and identify opportunities to improve efficiency, customer service, and profitability.

Financial Management & Strategic Planning

Develop and recommend long- and short-range plans designed to achieve the cooperative's purposes and strategic objectives.
Direct the financial operations of the cooperative and maintain accountability for the organization's financial performance.
Develop operating, capital, and cash budgets for Board approval and manage the business within approved financial parameters.
Provide regular, meaningful financial and operational reporting to the Board of Directors.
Monitor key grocery industry metrics and use financial and operational data to make informed decisions.
Identify new business opportunities and make recommendations to the Board regarding potential growth, partnerships, and innovation.
Participate in regional and national cooperative and grocery industry events to remain connected to emerging trends and best practices.

People & Culture

Determine the appropriate staffing structure and maintain clear, effective job descriptions.
Hire management personnel and oversee the hiring, training, development, and retention of Market staff.
Create a positive, productive, inclusive, and accountable workplace culture.
Manage and evaluate employees while providing timely coaching, feedback, recognition, and accountability.
Establish appropriate compensation structures based upon the budget, local labor market, and competitive conditions.
Organize staffing to promote a fair distribution of work while maintaining excellent customer service.
Develop and maintain an effective employee benefits program.
Build a culture where employees understand the Market's mission and their role in delivering it.

Marketing & Community Engagement

Develop and execute an effective advertising and marketing strategy that maintains strong public awareness of Gem City Market and its products and services.
Ensure marketing activities are executed within established budgetary guidelines.
Communicate effectively with cooperative members, customers, employees, community partners, and other stakeholders.
Prepare or oversee the preparation of the annual report and other communications to the cooperative's members and community.
Ensure that store displays, signage, promotions, and merchandising effectively support sales and customer engagement.
Strengthen Gem City Market's position as a trusted and visible community institution.
Identify opportunities to deepen relationships with local organizations, businesses, producers, and community partners.

Reporting Relationships

The CEO/General Manager reports directly to the Board of Directors
, which includes Market staff and members of the community.

The Board is responsible for establishing the organization's overall direction, goals, and expectations, while the CEO/General Manager is responsible for leading day-to-day operations and executing the strategy established by the Board.

The CEO/General Manager has the authority to hire, direct, structure, develop, and evaluate all other Market staff.

The successful candidate will understand the importance of building a strong, collaborative relationship with the Board based on trust, transparency, accountability, and open communication
.

Qualifications

The ideal candidate will bring a combination of grocery retail expertise, financial acumen, leadership ability, entrepreneurial thinking, and a genuine commitment to community.

Grocery Retail Leadership

Minimum of five years of successful experience managing a retail grocery store.
Strong understanding of grocery store operations and the various departments required to achieve sales, margin, labor, and profitability goals.
Demonstrated understanding of key grocery industry metrics and how to use them to drive performance.
Experience managing both retail and administrative functions.
Knowledge of current grocery industry trends and competitive dynamics.
Experience with merchandising and marketing in highly competitive grocery markets.

Financial Management

Demonstrated bottom-line accountability for a grocery or retail operation.
Strong understanding of financial variables and their relationship to overall business performance.
Experience developing and managing operating, capital, and cash budgets.
Ability to analyze financial and operational information and translate it into effective business decisions.
Demonstrated ability to balance affordability and customer needs with margin, cash flow, and profitability requirements.

Leadership & People Management

Proven ability to motivate, lead, and coordinate people to achieve organizational objectives.
Experience hiring, training, evaluating, developing, compensating, and, when necessary, terminating employees.
Ability to establish clear expectations and hold people accountable.
Strong listening skills and the ability to both give and receive constructive feedback.
Self-aware, self-motivated, and comfortable taking ownership of decisions and outcomes.
Ability to handle multiple priorities and demands while maintaining focus on the organization's most important objectives.

Cooperative & Community Leadership

Genuine understanding of and appreciation for the cooperative business model.
Ability to articulate what makes a cooperative different and how cooperative principles influence decision-making.
Experience working effectively with a Board of Directors.
Ability to build trust with Board members, employees, customers, and community stakeholders.
Service-oriented leadership style with a genuine interest in improving the community served by the organization.
Experience working in a food desert, food-insecure, or low-income community is highly valued.

Strategic & Entrepreneurial Thinking

Ability to make difficult decisions and take appropriate risks when necessary.
Strong problem-solving skills, including the ability to identify root causes and develop practical solutions.
Entrepreneurial mindset with the ability to recognize and pursue opportunities for innovation and growth.
Ability to maintain momentum and lead change with a sense of urgency.
Willingness to seek outside expertise and perspectives when appropriate.
Ability to balance immediate operational demands with the long-term health and sustainability of the cooperative.

The Opportunity

This is a unique opportunity for a hands-on grocery leader and community-minded executive
to lead an organization with a purpose that extends well beyond the four walls of a grocery store.

The next CEO/General Manager will have the opportunity to strengthen Gem City Market's financial and operational performance while helping fulfill its larger role as a source of affordable food, employment, connection, and opportunity within the Dayton community.

For the right leader, this is more than an opportunity to run a grocery store. It is an opportunity to help build a stronger community through grocery retail.

Interested candidates should contact Brett Myers, Managing Director of The Carlisle Group
, for more information regarding this retained search at bcm@tcgrecruit.com
.

jobs.description:
Position Overview:
The National Director of Operations leads the team of Operations Directors in each of the Project C.U.R.E. distribution centers throughout the U.S. Their primary role is to build, develop, encourage and grow the Operations Directors and their volunteer leaders in their abilities, accountability and effectiveness. Because Project C.U.R.E. is a volunteer-driven organization, identifying and developing the next generation of leaders is the paramount measure of success in this role. The National Director ensures that processes in each distribution center are carefully designed, consistently implemented, regularly audited and constantly improved, with the goal of delivering high-quality, life-saving medical supplies and equipment to underserved populations around the world.

Responsibilities:
The National Director of Operations is responsible for the development of the Operations Directors and their leadership team to achieve the mission of Project C.U.R.E. This is accomplished through coaching, mentorship, motivation, and accountability. An effective National Director will model these attributes and assist each Operations Director as they recruit, train and develop volunteer leaders who manage the thousands of volunteers that serve the organization.

The National Director will set clear expectations, provide direction, identify growth opportunities, and build a leadership pipeline of strong volunteer leaders who are identified, trained and promoted into greater responsibility. The Director establishes the training programs, meeting schedules, leadership standards and development pathways consistently across all locations.

The National Director of Operations will ensure that the Operations Directors achieve their goals and OKRs in these key areas:
Procurement & Transportation
– collecting the medical donations from local hospitals and clinics;
Equipment Inspection & Repair
– checking the equipment and repairing malfunctioning items;
Processing & Sorting
– checking quality of supplies, sorting into categories and boxing for shipment;
Warehousing & Safety
– maintaining the warehouses, trucks and equipment and providing a safe environment for staff and volunteers;
Packing & Shipping
– loading the containers with quality, appropriate cargo.

Qualifications:
A successful candidate has demonstrated success in both leadership and management. They understand operational details and can motivate individuals to achieve goals and metrics. They have a passion for international healthcare and the mission of Project C.U.R.E. They will demonstrate strategic thinking, rigorous execution, and the ability to inspire others both internally and externally.

The successful candidate demonstrates the following qualities:
Experience and Education:
Holds a bachelor’s degree and has 5+ years of operations, logistics or multi-site management experience, preferably within healthcare, distribution or a volunteer-driven nonprofit.
Develops leaders:
Builds, coaches and elevates direct-report leaders and the volunteer leaders beneath them, multiplying capability and creating a leadership pipeline within the context of a “performance culture.” Is accessible to volunteers and associates at all levels, interacting consistently, openly and honestly to ensure everyone is treated with dignity and respect.
Is goal oriented:
Manages to metrics, OKRs and Key Performance Indicators, including meeting or exceeding goals and objectives, monitoring performance and reporting results; is a “self-starter” who is internally motivated and does not require significant supervision.
Solves problems:
Can identify issues and create timely solutions to keep the mission moving forward, improve efficiencies and adapt to changing circumstances.
Works well with others:
Utilizes excellent relationship management and interpersonal skills; the ability to work effectively with donors, board members, volunteers, staff and interns; displays mature judgment, high emotional intelligence and effective communication skills.
Is a recognized leader:
Continually seeks learning and self-improvement, maintains the highest ethical standards and values, and encourages others toward higher levels of effectiveness.
Is a capable communicator:
Demonstrates effective communication skills in writing, interpersonal communication and public speaking; understands the importance of listening.
Is motivated:
Has an obvious passion and enthusiasm for saving lives and strengthening health infrastructure systems in the developing world, with an attitude of tenacity and determination.
Is well organized:
Is prepared, conscientious, effective and able to prioritize in an environment with multiple demands and complicated schedules.
Is coachable:
Has an attitude of openness, is eager to learn new things, and does not get stuck in a repetitive pattern of doing the same things the same way for too long. Can quickly comprehend complex concepts and will accept instruction.

Reports To:
The National Director of Operations is based at International Headquarters in Centennial, CO, and reports to the Vice President of Operations and Logistics.

Compensation & Benefits:
The National Director of Operations compensation range is from $95,000 to $100,000 commensurate with experience and ability. Compensation includes health, dental, vision, disability and life insurance. A 403(b) plan is maintained for employees.

About Us:
Healthcare in many developing countries is a global crisis. The severe lack of healthcare disrupts social and economic stability in almost every developing nation. Disease causes nine-out-of-ten preventable deaths in developing nations among children and adults. Millions of children under the age of five die each year from preventable disease, and more than 70% of these deaths occur from pneumonia, diarrhea, measles, malaria and malnutrition.

Founded in 1987, Project C.U.R.E. (www.projectcure.org) has grown to be the largest organization in the world delivering more than 250 semi-truck sized ocean freight cargo containers of donated medical supplies and equipment annually. Each project begins with an onsite Needs Assessment to ensure that Project C.U.R.E. delivers the right items to the right people. Project C.U.R.E. has delivered medical relief in 136+ countries. In addition, Project C.U.R.E. conducts C.U.R.E. Clinics, Helping Babies Breathe trainings, and bio-technical trainings to hospitals and health care clinics in 40 developing nations.

On average, the value of a Project C.U.R.E. Cargo container is worth approximately $400,000 (wholesale), providing an amazing 20-to-1 “return on investment." Project C.U.R.E. operates Distribution Centers in Denver, Phoenix, Houston, Nashville, Philadelphia, Kansas City and Chicago where 30,000+ volunteers sort more than 26,000 types of non-perishable medical supplies and certify medical equipment for shipment abroad. Project C.U.R.E. receives both new and quality used medical items from hundreds of hospitals throughout the United States and medical manufacturers, such as Stryker, Medline, Medtronic, KimberlyClark, Steris, and Hill-Rom.

Project C.U.R.E. operates on 2.5% administrative overhead and has earned numerous awards for being the industry leader in international medical donations. Project C.U.R.E. is recognized as a four-star organization by Guidestar, ranked a Platinum Participant by Charity Navigator and was ranked by Forbes magazine as one of the 20 most cost-effective nonprofits in the United States.

Mission:
The mission of Project C.U.R.E. is to identify, solicit, collect, sort and distribute medical supplies and services according to the imperative needs of the world.

• Partnership ~ We seek to assist other individuals and organizations that share our common vision.
• Creativity and Ingenuity ~ We will endeavor to pioneer new ways of meeting the needs of others, being stewards of our resources and solving problems—from the small inconveniences to the major obstacles.
• Stewardship ~ Despite the fact that most of our assets are donations, we will remember the source and value of these and treat each as a gift.
• Excellence in Service ~ We will do our best work in meeting the needs of one another, our donors, our partners, and the sick and dying around the world.

• Attitude ~ We will respect and honor others in the way that we treat them. We will strive to remain pleasant, positive and optimistic in all circumstances.

As Director of Business Development, you will help expand WSUS’s presence beyond our current customer set and build a qualified pipeline of opportunities aligned to M&C Saatchi World Services’ capabilities in strategic communications, behavior change, marketing, research, creative, digital, analytics, and public-sector advisory services.

You will be responsible for developing market insight, building and maintaining trusted partner relationships, identifying and qualifying opportunities, and helping position WSUS to win work as both a prime and subcontractor. This is not a siloed big-company business development role. You will work closely with WSUS leadership, capture, proposals, delivery leads, M&C Saatchi Group capability owners, and external partners. Identify, qualify, and advance opportunities across the Department of Defense, including military departments, defense agencies, combatant commands, and other DoD components, excluding health-focused DoD markets.

Bay Area Disc (BADA)’s mission is to serve, strengthen, and grow the Ultimate community by creating opportunities for athletes of all ages and backgrounds to interact, develop, and compete. BADA is more than just a sports organization. We believe in the transformative power of Ultimate as a tool for personal and community development. Ultimate isn’t just a game—it’s a vehicle for fostering connections, building character, and promoting inclusivity. Through Ultimate, players learn teamwork, leadership, and conflict resolution skills, all within a fun and supportive environment.
We serve a diverse community across the Bay Area, from young beginners taking their first steps on the field to seasoned adult players looking to refine their skills. Our programs offer a mix of recreational and competitive opportunities, creating spaces where everyone can find their place, whether they’re in it for the joy of casual play or the thrill of high-level competition. In addition to hosting our own leagues and tournaments, we partner with other organizations to expand access and foster even more opportunities for engagement.
Our vision is a Bay Area full of healthy, thriving, compassionate, and skilled individuals who live in strong, inclusive, equitable, and interconnected communities. By using Ultimate as our medium, we aim to cultivate these outcomes, shaping a future where people not only play together but grow together.
At the heart of BADA are our core values: Fun, Respect, Community, and Belonging.
These values guide our programs and initiatives, ensuring that we create environments where everyone feels welcomed and valued.
Bay Area Disc is a registered 501(c)(3) nonprofit dedicated to making a positive impact through sport, using Ultimate as a unique and powerful catalyst for change.

As the governing body that supports the sport in the region, we directly host leagues, tournaments and teams (often divided into youth and adult opportunities, with a mix of recreational and competitive opportunities), as well as partnering with other organizations to foster additional playing opportunities.

We envision a Bay Area full of healthy, thriving, compassionate, and skilled individuals who live in strong, inclusive, equitable, and interconnected communities. We use the unique sport of Ultimate to improve individuals and communities, creating the future we want to see.

About the Role

As the Executive Director of the organization, you’ll lead the entire nonprofit towards accomplishing its important mission and goals. Serving as the external face of BADA, the ED partners closely with the Board, the ultimate community, and the broader Bay Area community to secure and allocate the resources necessary to maintain the health of the organization and expand its programmatic impact. 
Reporting to the President of the Board, the Executive Director (ED) is the lead staff member who holds overall strategic, financial and operational responsibility for organization. This includes the management of the Bay Area Disc Association staff, fundraising, operations, donor cultivation, community engagement and organizational vision + development. The ED drives and is accountable for the execution of BADA’s strategic priorities and fulfillment of its core commitments. 
BADA has been serving the community since 2009, and was registered as its own 501c3 in 2018. The nonprofit is at a pivotal point in its maturity journey, and we’re excited for the impact that this role will have in leading an exciting new chapter, especially as we look to grow revenue through programming, grant, and donor funding, building on our strong programming base, so we can expand programming, deepen financial aid, and reach players and communities we don't yet serve.
BADA facilitates over 100 events annually, with approximately 5,000 youth and adult participants each year. These events range from local leagues and tournaments to community clinics and youth programs, providing opportunities for players of all skill levels. Our growth goals are deeply woven into our ongoing DEIB (Diversity, Equity, Inclusion, and Belonging) work, and we are centering inclusivity and accessibility as we move into the next phase. We currently have a team of 3 full time staff, with a broad network of contractors and volunteers supporting these initiatives as well. These folks all either directly or indirectly will report into this ED position.
This role is approximately 50% development, fundraising, strategic visioning to drive the organization forward, 25% internal operations, staffing + fiscal management, 25% programming + community engagement.

Classification: 0904 - Mayoral Staff XVI

Department: Mayor’s Office of Housing and Community Development (MOHCD)

Reporting directly to the MOHCD Director, the Deputy Director, Portfolio Management provides executive leadership for the City’s long-term stewardship of its publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and ensures equitable access to all City-sponsored affordable housing. The Deputy Director establishes strategic direction for asset management, affordable housing occupancy and placement, Inclusionary Housing policy, portfolio preservation, and regulatory compliance to ensure the long-term financial, physical, and operational success of the City’s affordable housing investments. The role also ensures that residents have safe, healthy homes that support the social, physical, and economic well-being of tenants and homeowners.

As a member of MOHCD’s Senior Leadership Team, the Deputy Director collaborates with executive staff to develop and implement agency priorities, establish organizational strategy, and advance policies that efficiently preserve and strengthen San Francisco’s affordable housing portfolio.

The Deputy Director provides executive oversight of the Portfolio Management Division that includes 25 staff members.

Additionally, The Deputy Director Directly Supervises Two Senior Leaders

Director of Inclusionary Programs and Housing Placement

The Director of Inclusionary Programs and Housing Placement is responsible for administering the City’s Inclusionary Housing rental programs, affordable housing marketing and lease-up activities, housing placement operations, and related occupancy functions. The Director oversees implementation of affirmative marketing requirements, resident selection processes, housing lotteries, and implementation of affordable housing preference legislation, policies, and procedures. The Director ensures occupancy procedures are compliant with local laws governing access to affordable housing and are equitable, transparent, efficient, and consistent across all affordable housing and homeownership opportunities.

The Director also provides executive oversight of the Database for Affordable Housing Listings, Information and Applications (DAHLIA) San Francisco’s affordable housing portal, and associated business processes supporting affordable housing marketing, application processing, resident placement, lotteries, and occupancy administration to ensure equitable outcomes for San Franciscans seeking affordable housing. The Director collaborates with affordable housing developers, property management companies, community-based organizations, and City departments to ensure consistent implementation of City housing policies and regulatory requirements including Fair Housing and the American Disability Act.

Director of Asset Managemen
t

The Director of Asset Management provides leadership for the long-term stability of over 36,000 rental and 3,000 homeownership units. The Director ensures financial and physical stewardship of MOHCD’s publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and works closely with project sponsors’ compliance staff to ensure the sustainability of all City sponsored affordable housing. Responsibilities include oversight of asset management, portfolio financial performance, multifamily loan servicing, capital planning, reserve management, multifamily refinancing and restructuring, rehabilitation planning, portfolio data management, financial risk assessment, and regulatory compliance. The Director develops strategies that preserve affordability, improve property performance, protect public investment, and support the long-term sustainability of the City’s affordable housing portfolio.

Role description

Essential Duties And Responsibilities

The Deputy Director’s responsibilities include, but are not limited to:

Serve as a member of MOHCD’s Senior Leadership Team, providing executive leadership on agency priorities, strategic initiatives, and organizational management.
Provide executive leadership and strategic direction for the 25-person Portfolio Management Division, ensuring alignment with MOHCD’s mission, priorities, and affordable housing objectives.
Supervise Director-level managers responsible for major programs and ensure effective coordination across all functional areas.
Establish division-wide goals, performance expectations, and operational priorities and efficiencies while fostering collaboration across all Portfolio Management functions.
Develop and implement equitable policies that strengthen long-term stewardship of the City’s affordable housing portfolio and improve organizational effectiveness while balancing the needs of the communities living in affordable housing.
Expand, standardize, and improve communication regarding City sponsored affordable housing operations, regulations and requirements among project sponsors, tenants and owners.
Oversee the long-term financial and physical performance of the City’s publicly assisted affordable housing portfolio and direct strategies that preserve affordability, protect public investment, and promote high-quality housing.
Provide executive oversight of affordable housing occupancy, marketing, lease-up, resident placement, housing lotteries, housing preference implementation, and DAHLIA operations to ensure equitable, transparent, and efficient administration of City affordable housing programs.
Direct policies governing inclusionary policy implementation, asset management, regulatory compliance, occupancy administration, resident selection, and portfolio preservation.
Oversee multifamily portfolio-related financing, recapitalization, rehabilitation planning, reserve management, and other long-term preservation initiatives.
Coordinate with affordable housing and private developers, property management companies, lenders, realtors, investors, regulatory agencies, community-based organizations, and other City departments to advance transparent affordable housing policy and operational excellence.

Reporting directly to the MOHCD Director, the Deputy Director, Multifamily Housing and Homeownership Programs
provides executive leadership for the City’s affordable multifamily housing production, preservation, housing finance, construction oversight, and homeownership programs. In coordination with the Director, the Deputy Director establishes the strategic direction for these program areas, oversees policy development and implementation, and advances innovative financing and programmatic initiatives that expand affordable housing opportunities and sustainable homeownership throughout San Francisco.

The Deputy Director provides executive oversight of the Homeownership and Multifamily Rental Housing Division that includes 38 staff members.

Additionally, the Deputy Director provides direct supervision to 5 Director-level leadership staff responsible for these major program areas:

New Construction
Acquisition and Preservation
Housing Finance
Homeownership Programs
Construction Representation

New Construction

MOHCD’s New Construction Program is led by a Director who manages a team of project managers and loan administrators responsible for developing 100 percent affordable housing throughout San Francisco. Responsibilities include underwriting projects for approval by the Citywide Loan Committee and Board of Supervisors; overseeing affordable housing development partners during programming, predevelopment, construction, marketing, and lease-up; administering the City’s Land Dedication Program; and closing construction and permanent financing.

Acquisition and Preservation

The Acquisition and Preservation Program is led by a Director responsible for financing the acquisition, rehabilitation, and long-term preservation of affordable multifamily housing. The program oversees refinancing and restructuring of existing affordable housing developments, administers the Small Sites Program, coordinates acquisition financing strategies, and partners with nonprofit developers, lenders, and public agencies to preserve affordable housing throughout the City.

Housing Finance

The Housing Finance Director is responsible for coordinating MOHCD’s multifamily financing and underwriting activities, including affordable housing revenue bonds, loan structuring, lending policies, capital financing strategies, and funding procurements. The Director evaluates federal, state, and local financing opportunities to maximize affordable housing resources and develops policies that strengthen the City’s affordable housing investment strategies.

Homeownership Programs

MOHCD’s Homeownership Programs are led by a Director responsible for the City’s affordable homeownership initiatives, including Inclusionary ownership programs within market rate housing and the sale and re-sale of Below Market Rate (BMR) units, first-time homeowner assistance programs, and related affordable homeownership opportunities. The Director oversees the secondary lending activities and administration of all homebuyer and homeowner loan programs including loan servicing of approximately 850 market rate property loans. Creating an average of 200 new first-time homeowners each year, the Director oversees the implementation of all homeownership programs generated by the Office of Community Investment and Infrastructure (OCII) and other affordable homeownership initiatives designed to expand equitable access to homeownership. The Director works closely with the Homeownership Compliance Manager to ensure households purchasing market rate housing with City assistance remain program eligible throughout their ownership. The Director develops and implements policies, oversees program operations, and collaborates with lenders, nonprofit organizations, developers, community-based organizations, and public agencies to advance the City’s affordable homeownership goals.

Construction Representation

A Senior Construction Representative manages a team of construction professionals responsible for evaluating MOHCD-funded projects throughout all phases of development to ensure cost efficiency, constructability, and compliance with program and design standards. The team monitors projects during construction through project closeout and works collaboratively with project sponsors and regulatory agencies to resolve development issues.

•Recruit and lead the Phoenix Ambassador Board, which is an engaged, active group of individuals who assist and advise the Executive Director in fundraising and development of the mission of Project C.U.R.E.
•Develop and manage strategic partnerships with organizations and companies as well as university programs, hospital partners, faith communities, and others; solicit funding, grants and gifts for Project C.U.R.E.’s projects around the world.
•Secure financial sponsors for individual container delivery projects through the C.U.R.E. Cargo program, and serve as the primary “Client Care” steward of that relationship throughout the project.
•Recruit and manage a team of volunteers and interns, including members of the Ambassador Board to expand the effectiveness of the Executive Director’s efforts.
•Collaborate with the Phoenix Operations Director who manages the procurement, warehousing, transportation, processing and delivery of life-saving medical supplies and equipment.
•Execute fundraising events in coordination with the Director of Special Events through securing financial and gift-in-kind sponsorships, donor attendance and event execution.
•Represent Project C.U.R.E. in the news and on social media as well as attend community events to increase the recognition and reputation of Project C.U.R.E. in the community.
•Coordinate with staff at the International Headquarters and the other Executive Directors in C.U.R.E. Communities by sharing stories and “best practices,” attending semi-annual Town Hall meetings in Denver, Colorado and participating in regularly scheduled meetings and conference calls.
•Manage accurate and up-to-date information on donors and other project sponsors in the Project C.U.R.E. (CRM) database.

Qualifications:
The Executive Director must demonstrate alignment with Project C.U.R.E.’s mission and core values, and possess the internal motivation and passion to address the healthcare inequalities in the developing world in a sustainable manner.

The ideal candidate for the position demonstrates the following qualities:
Is qualified:
Holds a bachelor’s degree and has at least five years of demonstrated fundraising success, specifically in the area of individual giving and major gifts.
Is goal oriented: Manages to metrics, OKR’s and Key Performance Indicators, including meeting or exceeding fundraising goals/objectives, monitoring performance and reporting results; is a “self-starter” who is internally motivated and does not require significant supervision.
Develops people: Recruits, inspires and leads volunteers, mentees and interns to achieve goals within the context of building a “performance culture.” Is accessible to volunteers and associates at all levels, interacting consistently, openly and honestly to assure everyone is treated with dignity and respect.
Works well with others: Utilizes excellent relationship management and interpersonal skills; the ability to work effectively with donors, board members, volunteers, staff and interns; displays mature judgment, high emotional intelligence and effective communication skills.
Is resourceful & “bottom line” oriented: To continue to meet the efficiency goals of Project C.U.R.E., the Executive Director must secure in-kind sponsorships and leverage relationships to reduce direct expenses by negotiating discounts and benefits with vendors and venues, and can meet budget and resource challenges to maximize net revenue goals.
Is a recognized leader: Continually seeks learning and self-improvement, maintains the highest ethical standards and values, and encourages others toward higher levels of effectiveness.
Is a capable communicator: Demonstrates effective communication skills in writing, interpersonal communication and public speaking; understands the importance of listening.
Is motivated: Has an obvious passion and enthusiasm for saving lives and strengthening health infrastructure systems in the developing world with an attitude of tenacity and determination.
Is well organized: Is prepared, conscientious, effective and able to prioritize in an environment
with multiple demands and complicated schedules.
Is coachable: Has an attitude of openness, is eager to learn new things without becoming defensive, and does not get stuck in a repetitive pattern of doing the same things the same way for too long. Can quickly comprehend complex concepts and will accept instruction.

Compensation & Benefits:
This position offers competitive compensation commensurate with experience and typically ranges from $95,000 to $110,000 annually. The position includes a generous health insurance plan, paid vacation and holidays, and a 403(b) plan.

: Healthcare in many developing countries is a global crisis. The severe lack of healthcare disrupts social and economic stability in almost every developing nation. Disease causes nine-out-of-ten preventable deaths in developing nations among children and adults. Millions of children under the age of five die each year from preventable disease, and more than 70% of these deaths occur from pneumonia, diarrhea, measles, malaria and malnutrition.

Founded in 1987, Project C.U.R.E. (www.projectcure.org) has grown to be the largest organization in the world delivering nearly 200+ forty-foot ocean freight cargo containers of donated medical supplies and equipment annually. Each project begins with an onsite Needs Assessment to ensure that Project C.U.R.E. delivers the right items to the right people. Project C.U.R.E. has delivered medical relief in 130+ countries. In addition, Project C.U.R.E. conducts C.U.R.E. Clinics, Helping Babies Breathe trainings, and bio-technical trainings to hospitals and health care clinics in 40 developing nations.

On average, the value of a Project C.U.R.E. Cargo container is worth $450,000 (wholesale), providing an amazing 20-to-1 “return on investment." Project C.U.R.E. operates Distribution Centers in Denver, Phoenix, Houston, Nashville, Philadelphia, Kansas City and Chicago where 20,000+ volunteers sort more than 26,000 types of non-perishable medical supplies and certify medical equipment for shipment abroad.

Ocean of Wisdom School (OWS) is a new K–4 public charter school preparing to open in Minnesota in Fall 2027, with a planned expansion to K–8.

OWS will combine rigorous, standards-aligned academics with Social, Emotional, and Ethical (SEE) Learning, fostering academic excellence, compassion, resilience, ethical decision-making, and a strong sense of belonging. The school will also incorporate Tibetan language and cultural learning as part of its globally grounded, culturally responsive educational model.

OWS is currently in its founding phase. We are seeking a Founding Executive Director to help turn this vision into a thriving school.

The Opportunity

As OWS's Founding Executive Director, you will have the extraordinary opportunity to shape a school's culture, community, and educational experience from the very beginning.

Working closely with the Board of Directors, the Founding Executive Director will lead OWS through the transition from planning to opening and establish the foundation for long-term success. The role combines educational leadership with organizational development, staffing, operations, financial management, enrollment, and community engagement.

The ideal candidate is energized by building something new, comfortable navigating ambiguity, and able to move between big-picture strategy and hands-on execution.

Key Responsibilities

School Leadership & Development

Lead the development and successful launch of OWS for Fall 2027.
Translate the school's mission and vision into effective educational and organizational practices.
Partner with the Board on strategy, governance, priorities, and organizational sustainability.

Educational Leadership

Lead development and implementation of a rigorous, standards-aligned academic program.
Integrate SEE Learning and Tibetan language and cultural learning into the school experience.
Establish systems for curriculum, instruction, assessment, student support, and continuous improvement.
Oversee special education services and related compliance requirements.

Staffing & Culture

Develop a staffing plan and recruit, hire, onboard, and develop the founding team.
Establish effective supervision, professional development, and performance-management practices.
Build a collaborative, inclusive, and mission-aligned school culture.

Operations & Finance

Establish the operational systems necessary to launch and operate the school.
Oversee compliance, contracts, vendors, risk management, and school-opening requirements.
Develop and manage the annual budget and maintain strong financial controls.
Support grants, fundraising, and other resource-development efforts.

Enrollment & Community

Develop student recruitment and enrollment strategies.
Build strong relationships with prospective and enrolled families.
Develop partnerships with educational, cultural, nonprofit, and community organizations.
Serve as a public representative and advocate for OWS.

Qualifications

We are looking for a mission-driven, strategic, and entrepreneurial educational leader who can turn vision into action in a startup environment:

Required Qualifications

Education & Credentials:

- Master's degree in Educational Leadership, Business Administration, or related field;
- Valid Minnesota administrative license (or eligibility to meet state qualifications)
Experience
: At least five (5) years of responsible leadership experience, with a proven track record of managing people, programs, and daily operations.
Academic Oversight
: Deep understanding of curriculum design, instructional best practices, student development, and special education compliance.
Financial Acumen
: Strong organizational and financial management skills, including overseeing complex budgets.
Stakeholder Engagement
: Exceptional communication and problem-solving skills, with the ability to effectively partner with a governing board, staff, families, and the community.
Mission Alignment
: A demonstrated commitment to whole-child education and the mission of OWS.

Preferred Qualifications

Startup & Charter Experience
: Previous leadership in the charter school sector, particularly experience founding, designing, or launching a new school or program.
Talent & Resource Development
: Proven success in recruiting and developing staff, as well as securing grants, fundraising, and building strategic community partnerships.
Educational Frameworks
: Familiarity with SEE Learning® (Social, Emotional, and Ethical Learning) or similar frameworks.
Cultural Responsiveness
: Experience with or knowledge of Tibetan culture, language, and culturally responsive education.

Position Details & Compensation

Position: Executive Director

(1.0 FTE)

Contract: Annual, renewable contract

Location: Minneapolis, Minnesota

Start Date: Anticipated early 2027 (ahead of Fall 2027 launch)

Salary: $74,000 - $80,000 per year, based on experience and qualifications.

Benefits: OWS is finalizing a competitive benefits package for our launch, which will include employer-sponsored health insurance and paid time off. Full plan details will be provided prior to the start date.

Application Process

To apply, please Complete the OWS Application Form and upload the following materials:

Resume: Highlighting your relevant leadership and professional experience.

Cover Letter: Sharing your interest in joining OWS and the specific impact you would make as Founding Executive Director.

Logistics & Timeline

Questions? Contact Ngawang Dolker, Board Co-Chair, at info@oceanofwisdomschool.org

Timeline: Applications will be reviewed on a rolling basis. The search will remain open until the Board identifies a strong pool of qualified candidates.

Note: Additional materials, including administrative licensure, educational credentials, and professional references, may be requested later in the selection process.
